A 69-year-old woman reports a 9-month history of occasional blood in her stool, which has become a
daily occurrence over the past week. She also complains of fatigue, shortness of breath, and mild

lethargy but denies weight loss, abdominal pain, or dietary changes. She follows a balanced diet and
does not use chronic medications or NSAIDs. Her vital signs include a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F),
pulse rate of 68/min, blood pressure of 151/69 mm Hg, and respiratory rate of 19/min. On examination,
she has pale mucosa and prolonged capillary refill time. Which of the following laboratory findings is
most likely for hemoglobin, hematocrit, RBC count, mean corpuscular volume, and reticulocyte count?
Answer Choices: (A) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count normal, mean corpuscular
volume ↓, reticulocyte count ↓ (B) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↓, mean
corpuscular volume↑, reticulocyte count ↑ (C) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↓,
mean corpuscular volume normal, reticulocyte count ↑ (D) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood
cell count ↓, mean corpuscular volume↓, reticulocyte count ↓ (E) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red
blood cell count normal, mean corpuscular volume normal, reticulocyte count ↓ (F) Hemoglobin and
hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↓, mean corpuscular volume↑, reticulocyte count ↓ (G) Hemoglobin
and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↓, mean corpuscular volume↑, reticulocyte count normal (H)
Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↑, mean corpuscular volume ↓, reticulocyte count ↑
(I) Hemoglobin and hematocrit ↓,  red blood cell count ↓, mean corpuscular volume↓, reticulocyte count
↑ (J) Hemoglobin and hematocrit normal,  red blood cell count ↓, mean corpuscular volume↓,
reticulocyte count ↑

reticulocyte count ↓
